text: The Ukrainian Air Force counted 570 weapons in the Russian strike of 1–2 July 2026: 74 missiles of five types and 496 drones of five types.
Kyiv was the main target of the Russian strike of 1–2 July 2026, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.
28 ballistic missiles flew at Kyiv on 1–2 July 2026, the most ever fired in one attack on the capital, according to Air Force spokesman Ihnat.

observations.note: record for one attack on Kyiv

text: The Ukrainian Air Force named the large number of jet-powered drones as a defining feature of the 1–2 July 2026 strike on Kyiv.
The 1–2 July 2026 strike on Kyiv came at the height of Ukraine's Patriot interceptor shortage of the e9b period.

The 1–2 July 2026 strike is the best-documented night of the 2026 strike war on Kyiv: type-by-type counts are published, the Air Force alerts are timestamped to the minute and damage is reported district by district.
On 7 September 2025, the record drone night of 2025, Russia launched 810 drones, 4 ballistic missiles and 9 cruise missiles across Ukraine.
On 7 September 2025 the Cabinet of Ministers building in Kyiv was hit for the first time.
On 7 September 2025 Sviatoshynskyi and Darnytskyi districts of Kyiv were struck and two people were killed in Kyiv.
The 7 September 2025 night would suit a drone-saturation chapter with a working Patriot shield, but it had few missiles and was spread across the whole of Ukraine.
On 19 July 2026, the record ballistic barrage, Russia fired 41 missiles at Kyiv in under an hour, 35 of them ballistic (25 Iskander-M/S-400 and 10 Zircon), plus 125 drones.
Only 18 of the 41 missiles fired at Kyiv on 19 July 2026 were downed, and one person was killed.
The 19 July 2026 barrage is a pure ballistic-defence puzzle with few drones.
On 1 July 2026 Zelensky warned from Dublin of an imminent massed Russian strike and flew home.
From about 19:30 on 1 July 2026, groups of Shahed-type and jet drones entered Kyiv Oblast from the north, east and south.
Jet drones were over Kyiv from about 22:50 on 1 July 2026.
On the night of 1–2 July 2026 a drone set the historic Zektser building on Shevchenko Boulevard in Kyiv alight.
At 01:12 on 2 July 2026 the Ukrainian Air Force warned of a ballistic threat from the north.

From 01:53 to about 02:31 on 2 July 2026, waves of ballistic missiles, Zircons among them, came in at Kyiv from Kursk Oblast (via Sumy and Chernihiv oblasts) and from Bryansk Oblast (via Chernihiv Oblast).
From about 02:50 to 03:50 on 2 July 2026, groups of cruise missiles crossed Sumy and southern Chernihiv oblasts and reached Kyiv from the north, east and south-east.
Banderol munitions and jet drones kept coming at Kyiv until the morning of 2 July 2026, many of them down the Kyiv Reservoir from the north.
On 1–2 July 2026 aviation, SAM troops, EW units, unmanned-systems units and mobile fire groups downed or jammed 524 of the 570 Russian weapons, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.
Only 4 of the 28 ballistic missiles fired on 1–2 July 2026 were stopped.
Hits were recorded in every district of Kyiv on 1–2 July 2026.
In Darnytskyi district on 2 July 2026 a missile brought down the end section of a nine-storey block.
The final toll of the 1–2 July 2026 strike was 31 killed and 102 injured in Kyiv city.
The Ukrainian Air Force published its type-by-type launch and interception figures for the 1–2 July 2026 strike as of 09:00 on 2 July.
On 1–2 July 2026 Russia launched 4 3M22 Zircon missiles from Kursk Oblast, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.
Of the 4 3M22 Zircon missiles launched on 1–2 July 2026, 0 were downed or suppressed (0%, our arithmetic on the Air Force figures).

Of the 24 Iskander-M/S-400 (ballistic) missiles launched on 1–2 July 2026, 4 were downed or suppressed (17%, our arithmetic on the Air Force figures).

Of the 34 Kh-101 missiles launched on 1–2 July 2026, 32 were downed or suppressed (94%, our arithmetic on the Air Force figures).

text: In total Russia launched 74 missiles on 1–2 July 2026, of which the Ukrainian Air Force says 48 were downed or suppressed (65%, our arithmetic).

On 1–2 July 2026 Russia launched 496 drones (Shahed piston and jet, Gerbera, Italmas, Banderol and Parodiya decoys) from Bryansk, Kursk, Oryol, Millerovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske (Crimea).
Of the 496 drones launched on 1–2 July 2026, 476 were downed or suppressed (96%, our arithmetic on the Air Force figures).
Of all 570 weapons launched on 1–2 July 2026, 524 were downed or suppressed (92%, our arithmetic on the Air Force figures).
On 1–2 July 2026, 25 ballistic missiles and 12 drones struck 33 locations, and drone debris fell at 18 more, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.
The Air Force's ballistic figures for 1–2 July 2026 do not quite add up: 28 launched, 4 downed and 25 hits.
Two of the 34 Kh-101s launched on 1–2 July 2026 are unaccounted for in the Air Force figures.
The Ukrainian Air Force said several missiles from the 1–2 July 2026 strike were "still being confirmed".
Ukraine's Defence Ministry gave rounder figures for 1–2 July 2026: "almost 500" drones and 77 missiles, 25 of them ballistic or hypersonic.
notes: differs from the Air Force's 74 missiles

text: Ukraine's Defence Ministry said over 90% of cruise missiles and 90% of Shahed-type drones were intercepted on 1–2 July 2026.
The outcome band for the 1–2 July 2026 strike is 91–92% of all weapons downed or suppressed, about 96% of drones and about 14% (4 of 28) of ballistic missiles.
The 1–2 July 2026 strike damaged more than 30 locations in every district of Kyiv.
At least 20 buildings in Kyiv were hit directly and nearly 100 damaged on 1–2 July 2026, according to PM Svyrydenko.
Part of a nine-storey block collapsed in Darnytskyi district of Kyiv on 2 July 2026.
64 apartments were destroyed in the partly collapsed nine-storey block in Darnytskyi, according to Zelensky.
The 1–2 July 2026 strike killed 31 and injured 102 in Kyiv city, according to DSNS on 4 July.
ISW and BBC reported 27 killed and 91 injured in Kyiv on 2 July 2026, an interim toll.
Ukraine's National Police reported "above 110" injured in Kyiv after the 1–2 July 2026 strike.
notes: exceeds the DSNS final figure of 102

text: In Kyiv Oblast seven people were injured on 1–2 July 2026, with damage in five districts and in Boryspil.
A record 52,500 people, including about 4,500 children, sheltered in the Kyiv metro on the night of 1–2 July 2026.
In June 2026 Russia carried out only two strikes of more than 300 weapons, on 2 and 15 June, against one to three a week in January–May 2026.
ISW suspects the June 2026 lull in large Russian strikes reflects stockpiling or a shift in production toward jet drones.
Kyiv's air-defence interceptor drones downed more than 500 targets in June 2026, and over 600 were downed or jammed in Kyiv Oblast, according to Syrskyi.
On 1 July 2026 the Air Force's Ihnat said Russia now flies jet drones "practically around the clock".
On 1 July 2026 Beskrestnov ("Flash") reported Gerberas with extra fuel tanks flying over Ukraine and back to Russia.
On the afternoon of 1 July 2026 Zelensky, in Dublin, said intelligence showed "another such massive Russian attack" was being prepared and urged people to use shelters.
Zelensky flew home early from Dublin on 1 July 2026 ahead of the expected massive Russian strike.
On 1 July 2026 WOG closed its petrol stations in Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast from 21:00 to 07:00 because of the threat of a night attack.
The Ukrainian Air Force's count of the 1–2 July 2026 attack starts at 18:00 on 1 July.
From 18:30 to 19:27 on 1 July 2026, drone groups crossed western Sumy Oblast toward Chernihiv Oblast, and drones in northern Chernihiv Oblast headed for Kyiv Oblast.
At 19:35 on 1 July 2026 a drone near Pereiaslav headed for Kyiv, an approach from the south-east.
At 19:54 on 1 July 2026 the first jet drones of the night, in Boryspil district, headed for Kyiv.
From 20:16 to 20:55 on 1 July 2026, jet drones headed for Vyshneve/Kyiv from the south-west, for Kyiv from the east, and past Dymer in the north.
Sunset in Kyiv on 1 July 2026 was at 21:12, and civil dusk at 21:59.
At 21:33 on 1 July 2026 jet drones were in northern Kyiv Oblast and western Chernihiv Oblast, heading south toward Kyiv.
At about 21:40 on 1 July 2026 Kyiv Independent journalists heard explosions and air-defence fire as drones were engaged on Kyiv's outskirts.
From 22:22 to 22:37 on 1 July 2026, jet drones headed for Kyiv from the north and for Brovary from the north.
The moon, about 97% lit, rose over Kyiv at 22:31 on 1 July 2026.
From 22:48 to 22:54 on 1 July 2026 jet drones were in the east and west of Kyiv, flying south.
At 22:58 on 1 July 2026 a jet drone changed course near Boiarka and turned toward Kyiv.
From 23:01 to 23:14 on 1 July 2026 more strike drones arrived from the north, and jet drones were over central and eastern Kyiv.
The first wave of the 1–2 July 2026 strike was drones on Kyiv's historic centre.
On the night of 1 July 2026 a drone set fire to the 1901 Zektser building (CityHotel Residence) on Shevchenko Boulevard in Kyiv, and firefighters worked there all night.
At 23:50 on 1 July 2026 drone groups along the Belarusian border in northern Chernihiv Oblast headed for Kyiv Oblast, while other groups headed for Mykolaiv, Kryvyi Rih and Poltava.
At 00:05 on 2 July 2026 drone groups, including jet drones, approached Kyiv from the north.
At 00:45 on 2 July 2026 Tkachenko of the Kyiv City Military Administration warned of a ballistic threat.
Around 00:45 on 2 July 2026 monitoring channels reported up to 10 Russian strategic bombers airborne.
At 00:50 on 2 July 2026 drone groups, including jet drones, were spread across Chernihiv Oblast heading for Kyiv Oblast, and more groups came from Sumy Oblast.
At 01:12 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force posted: "Threat of ballistic weapons from the north!"

text: From 01:53 to 01:55 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force reported four missiles heading for Kyiv from the north and through Sumy Oblast.
At 01:58 on 2 July 2026 two ballistic missiles from Kursk Oblast flew through Sumy and Chernihiv oblasts toward Kyiv.
At 02:00 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force posted: "Ballistic missiles approaching Kyiv from the east."

cites.quote: Ballistic missiles approaching Kyiv from the east.

text: Just before 02:00 on 2 July 2026 loud explosions shook Kyiv, audible deep underground.
At 02:04 on 2 July 2026 a ballistic missile headed for Kyiv from the north.
At 02:11 on 2 July 2026 strike drones approached Kyiv from the north and south.
At 02:16 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force reported probable Kalibr launches from the Black Sea.
From 02:17 to 02:21 on 2 July 2026 five ballistic missiles from Bryansk Oblast flew through Chernihiv Oblast toward Kyiv, about one a minute.
From 02:28 to 02:36 on 2 July 2026 missiles headed for Kyiv from the east and north, and jet and strike drones from the east.
From 02:37 to 03:03 on 2 July 2026 missiles crossed Zaporizhzhia Oblast toward Dnipro and Kryvyi Rih, then turned west toward Vinnytsia Oblast.
From 02:48 to 02:56 on 2 July 2026 missiles near Krolevets (Sumy Oblast) flew on a south-westerly course, then groups of cruise missiles flew west from Sumy Oblast into Chernihiv Oblast.
At 03:00 on 2 July 2026 a ballistic missile headed for Kyiv from the east.
BBC reported that on 2 July 2026 "a brief lull preceded another dozen cruise missiles at 03:00" over Kyiv.

cites.quote: a brief lull preceded another dozen cruise missiles at 03:00

text: From 03:01 to 03:17 on 2 July 2026 groups of cruise missiles crossed southern Chernihiv Oblast; at 03:17 the Air Force reported "missiles on the outskirts of Kyiv from the north, east and south-east".

cites.quote: missiles on the outskirts of Kyiv from the north, east and south-east

text: From 03:22 to 03:49 on 2 July 2026 more single cruise missiles came at Kyiv from the east and across southern Chernihiv Oblast.
At 03:47 on 2 July 2026 Klitschko reported six injured in Kyiv, all in hospital.
Around 03:47 on 2 July 2026 Tkachenko reported one dead in Kyiv, and the injured rose to 11.
At 03:59 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force posted: "Ballistic missile on Kyiv!"
Civil dawn in Kyiv on 2 July 2026 was at 04:05.
From 04:06 to 04:21 on 2 July 2026 Banderol loitering munitions approached Kyiv from the east and through Chernihiv Oblast.
At 04:15 on 2 July 2026 Klitschko reported a market in Shevchenkivskyi district burning after debris from intercepted weapons fell on it.
At 04:15 on 2 July 2026 Klitschko reported a five-storey block in Darnytskyi district burning and partly destroyed.
At 04:28 on 2 July 2026 a group of jet drones in northern Chernihiv Oblast headed south toward Kyiv.
At 04:42 and 04:58 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force warned of a ballistic threat from the south.
Sunrise in Kyiv on 2 July 2026 was at 04:51.
At 04:55 on 2 July 2026 Tkachenko reported two dead, 16 injured and 28 locations hit in Kyiv.
From 05:07 to 06:39 on 2 July 2026 jet drones were in western Kyiv, flew south over the Kyiv Reservoir (05:36, 06:30) and passed Kotsiubynske (06:17, 06:39).
Between 07:00 and 07:30 on 2 July 2026 more than 30 locations were reported damaged across every district of Kyiv, with nine killed and the injured rising from 34 to 56.
By 07:00–07:30 on 2 July 2026, 570 rescuers and over 125 vehicles were at work in Kyiv.
At about 08:00 on 2 July 2026 Klymenko reported 11 dead in Kyiv.
By about 08:00 on 2 July 2026 part of a nine-storey block in Darnytskyi was destroyed, and 17 people were rescued there, seven of them from the rubble.

text: At 08:20 on 2 July 2026 a jet drone was over the Kyiv Reservoir, heading south.
At 09:20 on 2 July 2026 the Air Force posted its 09:00 report: 524 of 570 weapons downed or jammed, and 25 ballistic missiles and 12 drones hitting 33 locations; "The attack is ongoing".
From 10:30 to 11:06 on 2 July 2026 new groups of jet drones flew from Bryansk Oblast into Chernihiv Oblast, and drones east of the Kyiv Reservoir headed for the capital.
On 2 July 2026 Ihnat said on Channel 5 that jet drones flying at up to 500 km/h are beyond interceptor drones, which fly at up to 300 km/h, so missiles must be used against them.
On 2 July 2026 Ihnat said the 28 ballistic missiles fired at Kyiv were a record.
Between 12:40 and 16:35 on 2 July 2026 the Kyiv toll rose to 18 dead (prosecutors), then 20 (Tkachenko), then 21 dead and 85 injured (DSNS).
On the afternoon of 2 July 2026, at the Darnytskyi site, Zelensky said at least 140 Patriot missiles are needed against about 70 ballistic missiles, and that partners' deliveries were late.
On the evening of 2 July 2026 Defence Minister Fedorov wrote to nearly 40 countries asking for Patriot missiles from their stocks "this month".
On the evening of 2 July 2026 Zelensky asked the US for licences to produce Patriot missiles.
On the morning of 3 July 2026 DSNS reported 30 dead in Kyiv after three more bodies were recovered in Darnytskyi.
Kyiv observed a day of mourning on 3 July 2026.
At 16:35 on 3 July 2026 the search of the destroyed nine-storey block in Darnytskyi was complete, with 10 bodies recovered there.

observations.subject: bodies recovered at the nine-storey block

text: On 4 July 2026 the final toll was 31 dead and 102 injured in Kyiv, and recovery ended at a 16-storey block in Darnytskyi.
By 4 July 2026 over 350 t of petroleum products from a petrol station in Obolonskyi district had reached Lake Kyrylivske.
On the night of 5–6 July 2026 none of 29 Russian ballistic missiles was intercepted.
At the NATO summit in Ankara on 8 July 2026 Trump said the US would license Ukraine to build Patriot interceptors; there was no timeline and the makers had not been told.

text: On 1–2 July 2026 the northern corridor ran from Bryansk across Chernihiv Oblast, or along the Belarusian border past Slavutych, then south down the Kyiv Reservoir or past Dymer; it was the main jet-drone and ballistic axis.

On 1–2 July 2026 an eastern and south-eastern corridor ran through Boryspil district and Pereiaslav.
On 1–2 July 2026 a south-western corridor carried drones looping in past Vyshneve and Boiarka.

text: Full moon was at 02:56 on 30 June 2026; on the night of 1–2 July the moon was about 97% lit, rose at 22:31 and was up for the rest of the night.
The near-full moon made the night of 1–2 July 2026 bright for visual and thermal spotting by mobile fire groups and helicopters.
The Ukrainian Air Force names the defenders of Kyiv on 1–2 July 2026 as aviation, SAM troops, EW units, unmanned-systems units and mobile fire groups.
No order of battle for Kyiv's air defence is public.
Col. Yurii Ihnat was the Ukrainian Air Force spokesman at the time of the 1–2 July 2026 strike.
Tymur Tkachenko headed the Kyiv City Military Administration, Vitali Klitschko was mayor of Kyiv and Mykola Kalashnyk headed Kyiv Oblast in July 2026.
Mykhailo Fedorov was Defence Minister and Oleksandr Syrskyi Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine in July 2026.
Patriot was the only answer to Russian ballistic missiles over Kyiv in July 2026; its battery count is not public and its interceptors were critically short.
Patriot and SAMP/T are the only Ukrainian systems able to intercept Iskanders, and a ballistic missile typically takes 2–3 interceptors.
Ukraine has about 1,000 Patriot missiles on contract, mostly for later years.
An April 2026 contract for hundreds of PAC-2s was backed by Germany, about 100 more were to come via a €1bn EU loan, and the first rounds came from European stocks.
Norway financed 200 Patriot interceptors for Ukraine, but "not a single one" had been delivered.
The US–Iran war used up to 1,430 Patriot rounds in 39 days, squeezing supply for Ukraine.
About 50 F-16s had been delivered to Ukraine by mid-2026, plus Mirage 2000-5s.
Ihnat said that against jet drones Ukraine must use fighter jets or SAMs.
Which Ukrainian aircraft flew on 1–2 July 2026, and how many sorties, is not reported.
IRIS-T SLM and NASAMS are in Ukrainian service; their role on 1–2 July 2026 is not reported.
Skynex batteries (four 35 mm guns with AHEAD airburst rounds, about 4 km reach) defend point targets against Shaheds.
Gepards defend point targets against Shaheds.
Kyiv's air-defence interceptor drones made more than 500 kills in June 2026.
In February 2026 interceptor drones made about 70% of Shahed kills around Kyiv.
The Sting interceptor drone flies at about 315 km/h and costs about $2,000.
The ZIRKA interceptor drone, unveiled on 1 July 2026, flies at 340+ km/h with AI auto-tracking and costs up to $2,000.
Ihnat puts interceptor-drone speeds at "up to 300 km/h" and says they cannot catch jet drones.
Mobile fire groups, MANPADS and anti-aircraft guns wear down Geran waves en route.
Ukrainian army aviation downed 338 targets in June 2026.
Helicopters take up to 40% of drones in their zones.
The Lima EW system's maker claims more than 20,500 Shaheds jammed.
Night Watch says EW accounts for about half of all "intercepted" Shaheds and missiles.

text: The Ukrainian Air Force's "downed/suppressed" figure combines kills and jamming.
DSNS had 570 rescuers and more than 125 vehicles in action in Kyiv by 07:00 on 2 July 2026.
The Kyiv metro sheltered 52,500 people on the night of 1–2 July 2026.

Russia fired 74 missiles on 1–2 July 2026, by Air Force type and launch area: 4 3M22 Zircons from Kursk Oblast, 24 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles from Bryansk and Kursk oblasts, 34 Kh-101s from Vologda Oblast, 8 Kalibrs from Novorossiysk and 4 Kh-59/69s from Voronezh Oblast.
The Kh-101s of 1–2 July 2026 were launched by strategic bombers, of which monitoring channels reported up to 10 airborne.

Russia launched 496 drones on 1–2 July 2026: Shahed-type (Geran) piston and jet drones, Gerbera, Italmas, Banderol loitering munitions and Parodiya decoys, from Bryansk, Kursk, Oryol, Millerovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske.
The jet share of the 496 drones of 1–2 July 2026 is not published; the Air Force and Ihnat called it "a large number", higher than in earlier packages.
Informational Resistance calls the 1–2 July 2026 strike "one of the largest ever" deployments of jet Shahed-238/Karrar types.
Jet Gerans (Geran-3/4/5) fly at 300–600 km/h.
Ihnat gives jet drones a speed of up to 500 km/h.
The Geran-5 has a range of about 1,000 km and a 90 kg warhead.
The Gerbera has a 2.5 m wingspan, an 18 kg take-off weight, a speed of 160 km/h and a 600 km range, and is used as a decoy, a scout or an attack drone.
Decoys made up 35–40% of Geran waves in 2026.
HUR estimates Russian output of about 3,000 Geran-4/5s a month (August 2026).
HUR estimated in June 2025 that Russia produces 60–70 Iskander-Ms and 60–70 Kh-101s a month, and 20–30 Onyx/Zircons.

text: Bomber wear limited Russian Kh-101 launches to 34 of a possible 92 in June 2026.
After a quiet June 2026, Russia probably stockpiled for the 1–2 July strike.
The Ukrainian Air Force called the "distinctive feature" of the 1–2 July 2026 strike the simultaneous use of many weapon types from many directions, with many ballistic missiles and jet drones.
Aviation analyst Dolintsev says using many weapon types in the same time window wears down the defence and makes the problem "exceptionally complex".

The 1–2 July 2026 strike ran about 16 hours in four phases: a drone and jet-drone prelude from about 19:30, a ballistic salvo with Zircons from about 01:50 to 02:30, cruise missiles from about 02:50 to 03:50, and Banderols and jet drones until about 11:00.
The sequence of the 1–2 July 2026 strike (prelude, ballistic salvo, cruise wave, Banderol and jet-drone tail) is documented by the Air Force alerts and BBC reporting.
Bryansk and Kursk are about 400 km from Kyiv, which gives short warning of ballistic missiles.
On 2 July 2026 the Air Force alert "two missiles from Kursk Oblast" (01:58) was followed by "approaching Kyiv" two minutes later.
Jet drones outrun interceptor drones and stress mobile fire groups, so missiles or fighters must be spent on them.
Almost all the Shahed-type drones aimed at Kyiv on 1–2 July 2026 flew on a new 3,900–4,100 MHz band, an apparent attempt to outpace Ukrainian EW, according to Beskrestnov.
From 2025 Gerans and Gerberas also used mesh modems.
Parodiya and Gerbera decoys flew in the mix of the 1–2 July 2026 strike.
The Gerbera has no modem or camera, so it holds a stable altitude and does not "trigger the alarm".
Zelensky's rule of thumb is two Patriot interceptors per ballistic missile (140 for 70).

Under the 2026 shortage, Ukrainian Patriot crews moved to one interceptor per ballistic missile, used manual mode so as not to waste interceptors on drones, practised shoot-and-scoot, and used decoys at about $30,000 each.
Ukraine's MoD says NATO After Action Review practice "more than doubled" Patriot effectiveness against manoeuvring Iskanders.
The Patriot result on 1–2 July 2026 was 4 of 28 ballistic missiles stopped.
Ukrainian ballistic intercepts fell to 10–15% in 2026.
Ukrainian ballistic intercepts ranged from 0% to 50% per salvo in 2026.
Interceptor drones, mobile fire groups, guns, helicopters and EW took 476 of 496 drones on 1–2 July 2026.
Ihnat said the drone interception rate was kept "above 90%" on 1–2 July 2026 despite the jets.
Zelensky put the September 2026 interception rates at 57% for jet drones and 70% for all drones.
44 of 46 cruise and air-launched missiles were downed on 1–2 July 2026; the kill per layer (SAM, fighter or gun) is not published.
About a week after 1–2 July 2026, three F-16s and a Patriot battery ambushed a Su-35; Russian channels said the Patriot radar cued the fighters.
notes: not part of the 1–2 July night

text: The F-16 and Patriot ambush of a Su-35 shows how scarce assets were combined in mid-2026.
Zelensky's public warning filled Kyiv's shelters on 1–2 July 2026: a record in the metro, and shelters fuller than ever.
Ballistic missiles caused the mass-casualty damage of 1–2 July 2026 in Kyiv: the Darnytskyi block, a crater by a kindergarten and the Nyvky crater.
Drones caused the hotel fire on Shevchenko Boulevard on 1–2 July 2026.
Debris from intercepts caused the market fire in Shevchenkivskyi district on 2 July 2026.

On the afternoon of 1 July 2026 Zelensky, in Dublin, said a massive strike was coming and flew home; WOG closed its pumps at 21:00, and that night 52,500 people went down into the Kyiv metro, the most in years.
From 19:54 to 23:14 on 1 July 2026, long before the missiles, jet drones probed Kyiv from Boryspil, Vyshneve, Dymer and Boiarka; at 23:14 they were over the centre and the east.
On the night of 1 July 2026 a drone set the 1901 Zektser building on Shevchenko Boulevard on fire.
In the ballistic hour (01:12–02:31 on 2 July 2026) a missile a minute came at Kyiv, from Kursk via Sumy and from Bryansk via Chernihiv, with "unbelievably loud" blasts heard deep underground.
During the ballistic hour of 2 July 2026 there were only enough Patriot rounds for a few of the incoming missiles.
In Darnytskyi on 2 July 2026 two missiles landed a few steps apart: one left a giant crater by a kindergarten, the other hit the end of a nine-storey block, which slid off the building's face.
People may have been sheltering in the basement of the Darnytskyi nine-storey block; ten bodies were recovered there over two days.
In the cruise wave (02:48–03:49 on 2 July 2026) cruise-missile groups tracked west over Krolevets and southern Chernihiv Oblast, then closed on Kyiv from three sides.
Of the 34 Kh-101s fired on 1–2 July 2026, 32 were downed.
At a Kyiv ambulance station on 2 July 2026, medics called out during the alert were hit on the way to their vehicles; nine ambulances were damaged and six crew injured.
From 05:36 to 08:20 on 2 July 2026 jet drones kept coming south over the Kyiv Reservoir and past Kotsiubynske under a setting moon.
In Obolon on 2 July 2026 a petrol station burned, and 350 t of petroleum products spilled into Lake Kyrylivske.
At Kyiv Zoo on 2 July 2026 glass from the dome fell on turtles and crocodiles.
A Red Cross warehouse in Kyiv holding UAH 79m of aid burned in the 1–2 July 2026 strike.

The Russian MoD said its 1–2 July 2026 strike hit "military plants" and Ukrainian defence and energy infrastructure in retaliation for "terrorist attacks launched by the Kyiv regime against civilian infrastructure" in Russia.

Euromaidan Press reports the Russian MoD framing the 1–2 July 2026 strike as retaliation for Ukraine's refinery strikes.

Peskov said only "military or quasi-military targets" were struck on 1–2 July 2026 and that Putin had been briefed.
Peskov added that Russia would "continue to increase pressure on the Kyiv regime".
